decisions.what: Tier 2 does the minimal gateway wiring: authorizeVehicle on the entry's tesla_id, Ref passed to the write ports. Tier 3 keeps the rest.
decisions.why: Tier 1 used the same pattern. The alternative merges tier 2 into the riskiest tier and makes one big review.

decisions.what: Update overwrites e.TeslaID from the Ref before any work, so resolveEnergy reads the proven car.
decisions.why: The module already overwrites caller values it owns (EnergySource, PriceSource). Without it, energy can be derived from an unproven car.

decisions.what: DeleteEntry becomes :execrows and Delete returns pgx.ErrNoRows on zero rows.
decisions.why: Update is :one and already reports not-found. The gateway maps a Delete error to a message, so a miss stops looking like success.

decisions.what: A manual-charge update or delete whose entry lookup misses answers 404, for both handlers.
decisions.why: A miss leaves no vehicle to authorize, and the ports accept only a Ref. design.md D8 claimed Delete is unreachable on a miss; the code proved otherwise.

decisions.what: fakeChargeWriter gained an opt-in linkedReader field so a successful Delete drops the row from the linked fake reader.
decisions.why: The D4 test asserts the entry present for the lookup and absent in the re-render, within one request. The alternatives weakened an assertion or rewrote the test.
